question: What is Ekam all about?
speaker: Sri Preethaji
verbatim_text: To us every human experience is sacred, we see that there is one human experience, one humanity. That is what Ekam means, it means oneness. Ekam is an enlightened state of consciousness where you are awake to the oneness of our existence. We are one with all forms of life. We are one with the universe. When you are not established in this great spiritual realization that we are one, your actions and behavior cause division and conflict.

question: Why did you feel the need to build a place like Ekam where people could come and find enlightenment?
speaker: Sri Krishnaji
verbatim_text: So both Preethaji and I, we travel across the world and we are co -creators of Ekam. is situated in Andhra Pradesh and it's a place for enlightenment. Our vision is to create 80 ,000 enlightened beings in this world, which is 0 .001 % of this population. And Ekam is a place which is a place for meditation and a place for divine grace. 8 ,000 people can meditate in Ekam at any given point of time. It's Asia's largest pillarless hall. And we travel to over 20 -25 countries each year addressing various sections of people. Leaders, business leaders, politicians, students, young leaders, women, men, everyone. Different sections. So wherever we travel, we see that young people in the world, they go through a lot of stress. And our vision is to teach the young people how to become free of the stress and how to live in a very beautiful inner state. So I'll come to what a beautiful inner state in a short while. But every one of them that we come across, there is tremendous amount of stress. And what is this stress? is about future.

That is the only reset button that can bring about every other shift globally and give us real lasting solutions.

question: How does stress affect us? What are the ways we handle stress wrongly?

It's killing us, it's killing our relationships, it is killing who we are, it is killing us from becoming who we want to become. So if we do not learn to handle this basic fundamental serious problem called stress, we will not be able to make it to the next level.

question: What is the relationship between inner state and outer success?
speaker: Sri Krishnaji
verbatim_text: So always Shri Pitajana, I say our vision is to create Buddhas driving eco-friendly benches with their loved ones. So Buddha here refers to your inner state, not the historical Buddha, but your inner state. No? And driving your eco-friendly bins is all the abundance you want in life. You want beautiful partner relationship, you want wealth, you want help, all this. And of course, you want all this to enjoy with your loved ones. It's not just for you, right? So that's our vision. So spirituality and success always go together. If you deny spirituality and only look at success, then very soon you will land in a place where life will be meaningless and purposeless. All the success you have created will not have any meaning or purpose. But when you add spirituality, which is your inner world to it, then whatever you have created has tremendous purpose and tremendous meaning. And you are actually enjoying doing it and living it. So that is the greatest contribution when you combine them both.

question: How would you define spirituality in one line?
speaker: Sri Krishnaji
verbatim_text: Spirituality is an inward journey where the path is very clear to become free of all stressful states or all suffering states, and to learn to live in a beautiful inner state. That is spirituality.

question: One habit that silently ruins our peace?
speaker: Sri Preethaji
verbatim_text: at the core of depression is a battle with oneself if we do not make peace with ourselves we will inadvertently criticize everything about ourselves about our appearance, our status, our home, our family, our life itself. When we are not at peace, we are at war. We are divided against our own sense. At the root of our inner conflict is the habit of incessant commentary. A commentary which divides every experience of our lives into should be or should not be. It is this habit that drives us to comparison. It is this habit that drives us to inner war.

question: Anger or attachment — which is tougher to let go?
speaker: Sri Krishnaji
verbatim_text: It is possible. But what have you become in the meanwhile? Have you ever brought attention to that? You have become a monster. Crude or sophisticated is the only difference. Expressive or suppressive is the only difference The Buddha once said Using your anger to hurt someone else Is like holding a burning coal in your hand With the intention of throwing it on others Not realizing it is burning your hand first You are mistaken If you think you are using anger No, it is anger that is using you Over the years you have become an intolerant, impatient and fault -finding human being. You would have lost loved ones or become distant from them because your anger would have provoked their anger provokes further anger. Don't ever imagine that you will give in to your anger and say what comes to your head while others have to take its sitting. It does not work that way. Your anger will make the other angry. It does not end in peace or any form of realization. Anger is the wrong fuel. It is like using crude oil to fly a plane.

question: Can sadness lead to spirituality?

The more you learn about awakening of consciousness and enlightenment, you will know the why of your unhappiness, the why of your suffering. You will discover the how of becoming liberated and living joyfully.

question: Is burnout a lack of rest or lack of purpose?
speaker: Sri Krishnaji
verbatim_text: I want you to ask yourselves three questions today on your quest for purpose. First question, what happens if you don't discover a purpose and don't ever live it? Do you want to know? Possibility one, without a purpose you lose passion. You may have great gifts and talents, but without a purpose, you would not find the courage to manifest your potential. You may have commenced your relationship from true love, but without a purpose, love disappears in the face of challenges, leaving you inwardly dry and lonely. Possibility two, without a purpose, you drive your career from a space of inner lack. You push yourself to achieve and to make money out of fear of becoming a nobody in the eyes of your loved ones.

question: What is the difference between the Beautiful State and the Suffering State, and how do they relate to each other?
speaker: Sri Krishnaji
verbatim_text: These are suffering states. In no suffering states, you have the beautiful states and the enlightened states. Beautiful states are states of gratitude, calm, peace, love. So when you're hurt, you dissolve your hurt, you move to love. When you're angry, you dissolve your anger, you move to peace. These are beautiful states. And then you have enlightened states, which are oneness and great compassion. Today, human beings are asking, what am I doing? But more important is, what is the state from which what I am doing.
